bug_info.bug_desc: When an instruction-fetch exception is delivered, the instruction queue reports the wrong faulting virtual address in fetch_entry_o.ex.tval. In the old code, tval is always taken from pc_q, the program counter of the instruction currently being emitted. For a 32-bit instruction whose two halves come from different fetch words, the page fault can occur on the second fetch word, so pc_q (the instruction start address) no longer matches the virtual address of the portion that caused the fault. The queue had no record of which fetch address actually faulted; it only stored the exception type and reused the delivery PC, violating the requirement that tval contain the faulting fetch address.
bug_info.fix_hint: Propagate the faulting instruction-cache virtual address from the frontend (icache_vaddr_q) into the instruction queue as exception_addr_i, store it in each queued instruction entry (ex_vaddr), and drive fetch_entry_o.ex.tval from that stored fetch address instead of pc_q when an exception is reported.
